question: Does the contextual constructor fail only because common specialization was applied to the substitution payload while retaining the unspecialized host/context, or does construction still fail when host, redex, and substitution are specialized coherently together?

arms.A_PAYLOAD_ONLY: Apply theta only to the source-law substitution and retain the original host term and path.
arms.B_WHOLE_CONTEXT: Apply theta to the source-law substitution and to the entire host term, retain the same structural path, then construct/lift the existing source-law equality in that specialized host.

decision_table.WHOLE_CONTEXT_RESCUES_CONSTRUCTION_AND_R: payload-only construction remains zero but at least one coherently whole-context-specialized item is constructible and replay-valid
decision_table.WHOLE_CONTEXT_CONSTRUCTS_BUT_REPLAY_FAIL: whole-context specialization crosses the constructor boundary but verifier replay rejects the resulting item
decision_table.WHOLE_CONTEXT_NO_RESCUE: common specialization remains semantically coherent but even coherent specialization of host, redex, and payload does not produce a contextual item
decision_table.PAYLOAD_ONLY_RESCUE_UNEXPECTED: the earlier zero-construction result does not reproduce

scientific_rule: This test changes only where the already-frozen common specialization theta is applied. It must not invent a new inference rule. A positive rescue establishes a state-transform compilation requirement, not theorem progress.
